parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime imposes universal-exposure measures at entry: passports are processed only as M/F per sex assigned at birth, a consular cable instructs officers to refuse cases where documents cast doubt on sex, and suspected misrepresentation can trigger a permanent fraud ineligibility. The state adds its own hostile layer: birth-certificate markers closed (surgical exception), documents that force outing, bathroom restrictions in state-run facilities with a documented trespass arrest of a trans woman, a minor-care ban, pronoun/disclosure laws, and no state gender-identity protections. That places the worst documented features at tier 1-2 universal exposure with partial but functioning national remedies. This sits materially below the 0.55 tier and slightly below the 0.35 anchors' clarity of exclusion, because enforcement is discretionary, several national orders are enjoined, courts work, and no credible custody-or-death pathway is documented for ordinary visitors.

entry_documents.exposure: Universal: national passport/visa markers must match birth sex; cable directs refusal on doubt and fraud analysis supporting lifetime ineligibility; reported confiscations stranding travellers; foreign governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Visa-fraud finding requires all four elements, never automatic; limited waivers; policy remains litigated; existing X passports valid until expiry.
entry_documents.interaction: State document rules (birth-certificate ban) interact with national entry screening to force disclosure of trans status at every checkpoint.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented national custody harms: corrections bureau conversion-style policies for transgender inmates, hormone denial; immigration custody forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Litigation ongoing; several orders enjoined; oversight record incomplete (reporting stopped).
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document discrepancy at entry can escalate to investigation, fraud allegation, detention and birth-sex custody placement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facility bans in government buildings across many states; this state's 2023 law restricts bathroom use in state-run facilities; documented capitol arrest, handcuffing, 24 hours in men's ward, up to 60 days' jail.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Trespass offence requires willful entry plus refusal to depart, with statutory exemptions; most states have no mapped ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State facilities law sits under national single-sex facility directives; criminal exposure arises only on refusal, not automatic arrest.

care_services.exposure: State ban on gender-affirming care for minors; national proposed rules barring public insurance reimbursement for under-18 care; hospitals subpoenaed for minors' records.
care_services.protection: Adult care access not documented as restricted in this state; national employment ruling partly operative.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor or parent could become an investigated subject; teachers facilitating transition face prosecution directives.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State party platform accused trans people of preying on women; national counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups; reward memo references 'radical gender ideology'; 190+ anti-trans bills in one session.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism powers stated not to target mere disagreement; 78% of residents support anti-discrimination law; governor condemned the platform.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing compounds national rhetoric, raising social-hostility risk for outed visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling minor faces state care ban, school pronoun/disclosure law allowing forced outing to parents, student-group discrimination allowance, sports bans; parent could face investigation exposure.
minors_guardians.interaction: National executive orders direct prosecution of facilitators, extending to transient families using schools or services.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No dated incident of anti-trans violence in this state documented; national hate-crime data shows sexual-orientation bias one-seventh to one-fifth of incidents; state hate-crime law excludes gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crimes statute covers gender identity; national employment ruling; city-level protections in one city.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to outed visitors depends on national statute given state-law exclusion.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Operative relationship of 2008 and 2023 birth-certificate rules unresolved; religious-refusal bill disposition unknown; no enforcement of the student-bill penalty documented; recourse at entry effectively absent for document refusals.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation ongoing; legal-aid FAQ for document rules; courts have enjoined several orders; appeals and waiver routes exist on paper.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation outcomes determine which exposures operate at travel time.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar universal-exposure structure: an entry regime that screens every trans visitor against birth-sex documents, with refusal and stranding documented and no effective real-time remedy. This jurisdiction adds criminal facility exposure and custody abuses the anchor lacks, but also retains more contested, enjoined, and discretionary enforcement.

The 0.55 anchor features discretionary secondary screening with administrative consequences. This jurisdiction is materially harsher: entry refusals are cable-directed rather than discretionary, the fraud ground threatens permanent exclusion, and the state layer adds criminal trespass and closed documents — so it must sit below that tier.

The 0.75 anchor has trained officers, tribunals, and compensation for unlawful detention. This regime lacks any comparable visitor-facing mitigation at entry or in state facilities, and documented custody abuse and facility bans exclude it from that band entirely.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces a combined regime whose entry stage is a universal exposure: birth-sex markers, doubt-based refusals, and a fraud ground with lifetime stakes, corroborated by foreign travel advisories and reports of stranding. The state layer compounds rather than offsets this — closed birth-certificate markers that force disclosure, bathroom restrictions with a documented arrest and brief custodial placement, a minors' care ban, and no state gender-identity protections — placing it among the worst-rated states in the national assessment. Offsets are real but partial: courts function and have enjoined several orders, the fraud finding is not automatic, the trespass offence requires refusal to depart, and national hate-crime and employment protections remain. No execution or routine imprisonment pathway is documented for visitors, but the escalation chain from document check to detention to birth-sex custody is documented nationally. Universal-exposure severity plus documented state hostility without effective local remedy yields a score in the High Risk band.
